description: The configuration surface of the seaweedfs chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

gateway.description: The S3 gateway — docs/plan/15's ADR-008: "the API is S3".

replicas.description: Number of S3 gateway pods. The gateway is stateless, so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

imageName.description: Override the full image reference, tag included. Empty means chrislusf/seaweedfs:{version}, which is what keeps version upgrades a property rather than an escape hatch.
imageName.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: The operator supplies NO default image at all — api/v1/image.go returns an empty image unchanged — so spec.image is always written. A pinned reference here defeats the version property, so it is a platform escape hatch rather than a tenant setting.

masters.description: Number of master servers. The masters hold the volume topology in a Raft group, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

enabled.description: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor per component. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". Turning it off removes the metrics port as well as the scrape, which is the operator's own behaviour rather than this provider's.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

replication.description: Where the second copy of every object is placed. None keeps one copy and is for scratch data only. A placement the cluster's topology cannot satisfy leaves volumes read-only rather than failing the create. Immutable, because SeaweedFS applies this to volumes as they are created and never rewrites the ones that already exist — a change would split the account into two durability promises with no way to tell which object got which.

sizing.description: CPU and memory per volume server, either by preset or explicitly. The masters, the filer and the S3 gateway are sized by the platform and are not affected.

cpu.description: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

memory.description: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

preset.description: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Volume servers use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

storage.description: The data volume, per volume server.

class.description: StorageClass name for the volume servers. Empty means the cluster default.

size.description: Data volume size per volume server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

version.description: SeaweedFS version. ⚠ SeaweedFS ships a release roughly weekly and maintains no long-term branch, so docs/plan/12's "supported major versions" is a shape this project does not have; the two values here are the two most recent releases and a new api-version is what adds a third.

volumeServers.description: Number of volume servers. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the volume size below, before replication.
